comment: What each Linux build adds on top of the upstream release it is made from.
The key is the full tag without its release- prefix, as in 3.6.6-linux1.
generate-release-notes.ts turns the entries into a section of the release
notes, above the upstream changelog. Leaving a version out of this file is
fine: the section is then left out too.
This file is ours. It sits next to the upstream changelog.json rather than
inside it, so that merging an upstream release never conflicts here.

3.6.11-linux2: "Show in your File Manager" brings the file manager to the front when it shows a repository, under Wayland too, where it only asked for attention in the task bar: the repository opens with its .git entry selected when hidden files are visible, and with nothing selected otherwise

Otherwise the same application as 3.6.11-linux1, including its security update: the bundled Git 2.56.1 fixes six vulnerabilities, the most serious letting a malicious repository run code when it is cloned along with its submodules: <https://github.blog/open-source/git/git-security-vulnerabilities-announced-7/>
The bundled git keeps its commands as links, as in earlier builds: upstream copies them in full instead, which doubles the size of the installed app
Also available as a Flatpak, from the package repository or as a .flatpak file: either way, flatpak update brings the versions that follow
The package repository serves the .deb, the .rpm and the Flatpak, and keeps them up to date through apt, dnf, zypper or flatpak: <https://packages-github-desktop.nitramo.fr/>
The window shows its own icon under Wayland, and groups with its launcher in the taskbar
Ptyxis is detected as a terminal, along with the editors and shells upstream added since 3.4.13
3.6.11-linux1: Security update, recommended for every channel: the bundled Git moves to 2.56.1, which fixes six vulnerabilities. The most serious lets a malicious repository run code on the machine when it is cloned along with its submodules, which is how GitHub Desktop clones. GitHub Desktop uses its own Git, so updating the Git of the system does not cover it: <https://github.blog/open-source/git/git-security-vulnerabilities-announced-7/>

"Show in your File Manager" asks the file manager already running to show the folder, instead of starting it again: Dolphin opens it in a new tab when set to, rather than in a new window holding the tabs of its last session
The bundled git keeps its commands as links, as in earlier builds: upstream copies them in full instead, which doubles the size of the installed app
Also available as a Flatpak, from the package repository or as a .flatpak file: either way, flatpak update brings the versions that follow
The package repository serves the .deb, the .rpm and the Flatpak, and keeps them up to date through apt, dnf, zypper or flatpak: <https://packages-github-desktop.nitramo.fr/>
The window shows its own icon under Wayland, and groups with its launcher in the taskbar
Ptyxis is detected as a terminal, along with the editors and shells upstream added since 3.4.13
3.6.10-linux1: Follows 3.6.7-linux1: no Linux build was made from upstream 3.6.8 and 3.6.9, so this one also brings their changes, listed only in their own release notes: <https://github.com/desktop/desktop/releases/tag/release-3.6.8> and <https://github.com/desktop/desktop/releases/tag/release-3.6.9>. Among them: short-lived tokens for new sign-ins, Git 2.56.0, Electron 44.9.1, SSH host key prompts that work with newer OpenSSH, and no more crash when Copilot stops unexpectedly
